newsitem.title: USA: Autonomous laser eye surgery surge. [CORRECTED 23:07 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Autonomous laser eye surgery surge. [CORRECTED 23:07 GMT]

text.p: Autonomous Technologies Corp expects the number of laser vision correct surgical procedures in the U.S. to shoot up to 200,000 in 1997 from 108,000 (corrects from "180,000") last year, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Randy Frey said.
Speaking at the Cruttenden Roth Growth Stock Conference here, Frey estimated the size of the worlwide laser vision correction market at between $1 billion and $5 billion.

Autonomous Technologies is developing new systems to simplify laser eye surgery procedures. Its LADARVision is a high-speed laser radar eye tracking system which it says will allow doctors to use low-power small beams in surgery, resulting in reduced trauma and improved outcomes.
Frey said that as the company works to bring this technology to the market, its cash on hand should last through the end of 1997, and it will need additional financing for 1998.
